analysis: Examined three changes. (1) docs/provider/troubleshooting.md is documentation only: the date bump, a reworded `usage reporting` row (head line 87) and a new `Requests served` troubleshooting row (head line 144). The new row says the local status counter includes cancelled and dropped requests and free self-route requests, and that Earnings lists only paid jobs. It describes counters only. It grants no trust, changes no authorization or attestation behavior, and exposes no secrets or prompt content. It does not touch the T-041 cache posture or the App Attest and authorization threats. (2) provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/ProviderLoop+Trust.swift adds `cancellationsPartialComplete: stats.cancellationsPartialComplete` to the DaemonState.Stats built in currentDaemonState (head ~lines 69-70). This is a numeric counter written to the local daemon-state.json, which is owner-scoped diagnostics for the status/doctor CLI. Prompt content is not involved, nothing is sent to the coordinator, and no new trust decision depends on it. Leakage is limited to an aggregate count, in line with the existing request and token counters. Integration questions outside the supplied evidence: the definition of `stats.cancellationsPartialComplete` and the DaemonState.Stats initializer/Codable change are not in this batch. The reader in StatusCommand+ServedRequests.swift is also not supplied. I verified neither that the new field is optional or defaulted for decoding older state files, nor that it is incremented consistently. Those are correctness and compatibility matters, not demonstrated security regressions. I did not see any change to cancellation propagation (T-010), so the counter is observational only.
